trace_analysis.timeout_class: recoverable turn-budget exhaustion, not final test timeout
primary_causes: Four implement turns reached the 900 second Octos cap: REQ-2.2, REQ-4.2.1, REQ-6.1.1 and REQ-6.1.2; REQ-6.1.3 also reached the cap and required rewrite/repair.
The 51000 second global budget was not the limiting value; individual turns and tool-heavy debugging were the bottleneck.
REQ-5.5.2 was interrupted by an upstream proxy HTTP 400 unexpected EOF, not by application behavior.
Repair turns repeatedly hit a ten-request guard and several acceptance attempts hit ConnectionResetError on /favicon.ico while the backend was still running.
Postflight killed 196 stray processes; cgroup peak was about 1.08GB against a 2GB limit, with no OOM event.
optimization_opportunities: Use a shorter per-node implementation budget or explicit stop-and-verify checkpoints before the 900 second cap.
Reserve repair budget for the nodes with concrete test failures; avoid repeated full-file exploration and full rewrites.
Use stable PID-scoped server cleanup and make unknown paths return 404, preventing favicon connection resets from poisoning acceptance rounds.
Separate structural checks from full acceptance and avoid spending 106 tools on a single late node such as REQ-5.6.1.
Treat provider proxy errors as retryable infrastructure events with bounded backoff rather than consuming a feature repair cycle.
trace_analysis.final_effect: All six intermediate failures were repaired or retried successfully; no final functional failure remains.
